target.title: fix(commands): bound reset-hook transcript reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadBeforeResetTranscript` in `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.ts` reads session transcript JSONL files with unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` calls. A runaway or corrupted transcript file could force the `before_reset` hook path to buffer the entire file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reset-hook transcripts are line-oriented JSONL files. A 16 MiB cap is generous headroom for long sessions while preventing the reset hook path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector. When the cap is exceeded, the hook fires with empty messages, matching the existing fallback behavior for unreadable files.

## User Impact

`before_reset` hooks now safely skip oversized transcripts instead of risking process OOM.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that writes a transcript exceeding the 16 MiB cap, mocks a `before_reset` hook runner, and asserts the hook fires with empty messages.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.test.ts --run` passes (13/13 tests).


## Real behavior proof

I ran the reset-hook transcript regression tests, including the archived-transcript recovery case and the bounded-read case. The before-reset hook path now reads through `readRegularFile` with a 16 MiB cap:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-core.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |auto-reply| src/auto-reply/reply/commands-core.test.ts (5 tests) 219ms
     ✓ recovers the archived transcript when the original reset transcript path is gone
     ✓ keeps leaf-controlled side branches out of before_reset hooks
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.96s
```

The 16 MiB cap prevents a runaway reset transcript from OOMing the reset hook path while preserving the existing archived-transcript fallback behavior.
